DO_NOT_CITE: This FAR was withdrawn from the README and ETHICS.md. It is kept as the record of a discarded attempt, not as a result.
retraction_reason: FairFace repeats individuals and labels those repeats inconsistently, so 'impostor' pairs are contaminated by genuine same-person pairs. Image-level deduplication catches the same SHOT twice, never the same person at a different event, and deduplicating on face similarity would be circular -- it removes the very false accepts being counted. The max impostor score here is +0.6400, which is a same-person pair that survived every filter.
what_is_claimed_instead: scripts/demo_negative_control.py: 0 false accepts in 11 real web candidates with known identities, at a 3x threshold margin. Trustworthy, not demographic.
dataset: FairFace 1.25 validation (labels supplied by the dataset)
measures: cross-group false accept rate only. False rejects need identity-paired data (RFW/BUPT), which is access-gated. WITHIN-group FAR is not reported: FairFace repeats individuals, so same-group pairs are contaminated by genuine same-person pairs -- verified by inspecting the top-scoring pairs, which are visibly the same people.
per_group_spread_note: 11 false accepts across 7 groups (0,0,1,2,2,2,4). Expected ~1.6 per group under a constant rate; Poisson variation covers every observed value, and re-running flipped the ordering. Do NOT read the per_group FAR values as a bias ranking -- the aggregate is the only figure this sample supports.
caveat: FairFace race/gender labels are annotation conventions, not biological facts, and no attribute is inferred from any face here. Cross-group pairs are the EASY case; this understates the disparity that within-group pairs would reveal, and that measurement is not available from this dataset.
